text:
alice.k: FYI — dedicated capacity commit for team Echo in eu-west-1 just hit the configured threshold (100% committed GPUs) and the admission controller started pulling back requests. Seeing queue depth spike in the last 2m.

ben_m: Confirming. Grafana shows `reserved_commit_utilization: 1.00` and `inflight_queue_len` jumped from ~10 to 420.

carla-ops: Is soft-throttle mode enabled or did it switch to hard admission?

sre-bot: [automated] Policy check: CommitID=echo-prod-2026-03, Mode=soft_throttle -> started shedding low-priority requests.

alice.k: It flipped to soft throttle, but downstream backpressure is still causing retries and we’re seeing error amplification on clients.

mike_oncall: Runbook step 1: identify low-priority routes and apply immediate priority-tag override. Can someone paste the routes list?

ben_m: Quick list: `/v1/generate` (high), `/v1/embeddings` (medium), `/v1/batch-infer` (low), `/v1/logprob` (low).

carla-ops: I’ll patch routing to drop `batch-infer` and `logprob` to best-effort. Doing `kubectl patch` now.

carla-ops: ```
kubectl -n redwood patch configmap admission-policy --type merge -p '{"data":{"priority_overrides":"batch-infer=best-effort,logprob=best-effort"}}'
```

sre-bot: [automated] Configmap patch applied by carla-ops at 2026-03-18T09:12:23Z

alice.k: Thanks. Also enabling fallback routing to hosted pool for non-sensitive datasets — need a ttl on that fallback.

ben_m: Can we open a temporary spare burst in eu-west-1? Reserved pools are all committed — we could activate cross-region borrowing (slow path) or spin up ephemeral on-demand. Cost tradeoff obvious. Thoughts?

mike_oncall: Prioritize cross-region borrow to avoid spin-up latency. Set `max_cross_region_borrow=50%` for priority=high only.

carla-ops: Pushing cross-region borrow: ```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/pools/borrow -d '{"from":"eu-west-1","to":"eu-central-1","percent":50,"routes":["/v1/generate"]}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN'
```

sre-bot: [automated] Borrow request accepted; bootstrap job queued (eta ~45s).

ben_m: Monitoring queue now. If borrow succeeds we should see inflight queue shrink. If not, we need to widen scope and consider on-demand GPUs (will hit cost).

alice.k: Also toggle admission controller policy to be slightly more permissive for cached KV hits. We have a lot of prefix cacheable requests — that should lower token work.

carla-ops: Patch admission: `allow_cached_hits=true` for commit=echo-prod-2026-03. Pushing.

mike_oncall: Good. Also notify Echo product team about possibility of transient higher latencies/call failures. 

alice.k: Notifying product: `@echo-team` in #customer-notify with short note.

ben_m: Quick query showing effect: `sum(inflight_queue_len{commit="echo-prod-2026-03"}) by (route)` -> `/v1/generate` down 60% after borrow job started. `/v1/embeddings` still climbing.

carla-ops: Embeddings are medium priority — recommend moving them to on-demand hosted until commit stabilizes.

mike_oncall: Do it. Carla, if you trigger hosted fallback for embeddings, add quota cap so cost doesn't explode. Set cap=200000 tokens/hr.

carla-ops: Triggered hosted fallback with quota cap. Response: `fallback-id=fb-7862`

sre-bot: [automated] Fallback route active: `/v1/embeddings` -> hosted (cap=200000 tokens/hr).

alice.k: After these mitigations: queue depth steadying at ~35, admission rejects down to nominal. Borrow completed and cross-region latency within SLO for high-priority calls.

ben_m: Action items: 1) Ops to leave cross-region borrow active for 30m 2) Product to throttle non-critical pipelines 3) Cost team to retroactively analyze on-demand charges if we spin up ephemeral GPUs.

carla-ops: I’ll set borrow TTL=30m, confirm.

carla-ops: TTL set. Also created a short-lived incident ticket: `INC-2026-0423` with summary and timeline.

mike_oncall: Closing loop — set a postmortem trigger if similar event happens within 7d. We may need adjustable commit thresholds and pre-warm signals for planned ramp-ups.

alice.k: Agreed. Suggestion for follow-up RFC: add predictive autoscaling hooks to reserved capacity (based on 10m rate-of-change).

ben_m: Adding to backlog. For now monitoring and cost guards look good. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: [automated] Thread archived to incidents on channel `incidents` by carla-ops at 2026-03-18T09:27:58Z
